_comment: Every GitHub Action in .github/workflows/ whose owner is not GitHub's own
platform must appear here. A third-party action runs over this repository
with a token on every pull request, so accepting one is a §5 boundary
decision; this file is where that decision is recorded, and
tests/security/test_third_party_actions.py fails when an action is pinned
without a record or when its MAJOR version moves past the reviewed one.
Why major and not every SHA: Dependabot bumps actions daily, so requiring a
human review per SHA would fire on routine patches and be switched off --
the failure mode AGENTS.md names for a rule that fires too often. A major is
where an action's internals change, which is also why #316 made majors
arrive as their own pull request.
For an 'accepted_unreviewed' entry, reviewed_version and reviewed_sha record the
pin it is grandfathered at -- not a review that happened.
status is 'reviewed' only when a human read the action's own definition at
the recorded SHA. 'accepted_unreviewed' is grandfathered debt: pinned and
bounded, but nobody has read it. That distinction is the point of this file
-- seeding every entry as 'reviewed' would assert what was never measured.
All four entries now read 'reviewed' (2026-11-05). That is NOT a claim that
the vendor code is benign: every record names what was not read, and for all
four that includes the bundle or image the action actually executes. What a
review establishes is provenance and blast radius, not safety. The status
exists so the next reader can tell a measurement from an assumption, and
'accepted_unreviewed' remains the correct status for anything added later
and not yet read -- the gate still enforces that such an entry claims
nothing verified, driven against a planted record so the rule is exercised
even while no shipped entry carries that status.
Each record also declares `execution`: what actually runs (runs.using, the
entrypoint, any pre/post hook) and whether our 40-hex pin fixes it. For a
composite or node action it does -- the steps, or the bundled dist/
entrypoint, are in the vendor's tree at that commit. For a DOCKER action it
may not: the pin fixes action.yml, and action.yml names an image.
ossf/scorecard-action names `docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.5.0`,
a mutable tag, so whoever can push that tag chooses the code this repository
executes -- and no SHA pin, Dependabot bump or permissions gate can see a tag
move. The test DERIVES pinned_by_sha from the entrypoint and compares it with
the declaration, so a record cannot claim a pin it does not have, and a
record with a gap must state it in pin_gap.

actions.reviewed_in: #320 (owner accepted 2.2.0 on 2026-11-05; the review itself is recorded here)
actions.reason: Dependency capability diff on every pull request; agent-config audit by manual dispatch only.
properties_verified: runs.using is composite: no Docker image, no JS entrypoint
no pre: or post: hooks
inputs reach the shell only through env:, never ${{ }} inside run:
base-ref is allow-listed against option injection before git sees it
--end-of-options on every git call
the nested github/codeql-action/upload-sarif is itself SHA-pinned
the comment script's API calls are scoped to repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/
mode: deps performs no package-registry fetch; the npm ci is in the agents branch only
exactly one runtime dependency (yaml)
not_reviewed: bin/penthera.js and the bundled scanner it runs -- thousands of lines of bundled JavaScript. Neither #305's review of 1.9.0 nor this one audited it, and this record does not claim otherwise. What bounds it is the list below, not a reading of the code.
bounded_by: fail-on: none, so findings never fail the step
the workflow is not one of §8's required checks
two write grants only (pull-requests for one comment, security-events for one SARIF upload)
mode: scan is structurally excluded and mode: agents is reachable only by manual dispatch
penthera-version asserts 2.2.0, so a re-pointed ref fails closed -- a vendor-supplied layer
tests/security/test_third_party_actions.py, which fails if this pin's major moves past 2
actions.notes: Reviewed at a9bbcab4 on 2026-11-05 by reading action.yml at that commit, verified as the commit the v2.2.0 tag names. All nine properties #305 established for 1.9.0 still hold, and two tightened: base-ref now also refuses `..` ranges, and the action exits 2 when it wrote no report rather than passing silently. Upstream changed nine exit codes in 2.2.0; for this repository's usage (mode: deps, fail-on: none, non-required job) they only make the job more likely to go red, which is the safe direction. The jump was two majors, 1.9.0 to 2.2.0; Dependabot's #314 proposed it bundled with a setup-uv patch and was closed unmerged, and #316 has since moved majors out of the group so the next one arrives alone.

actions.reason: Installs uv for the lock-sync gate. Predates this file; pinned and in use since before the record existed.
properties_verified: runs.using is node24 with main: dist/setup/index.cjs -- no Docker image, so the 40-hex pin fixes the code that runs
a post: hook EXISTS -- dist/save-cache/index.cjs with post-if: success() -- which runs after the job with the same token. There is no pre: hook
27 inputs are declared and OUR STEP PASSES NONE, so every default applies; the top-level keys are name, description, author, inputs, outputs, runs, branding, with no nested action
download-from-astral-mirror defaults to "true", so by default the uv binary is fetched from Astral's own mirror rather than from GitHub releases
checksum is an optional input and we pass none, so this repository pins no checksum for the binary that then resolves and installs its whole dependency tree
github-token defaults to ${{ github.token }}; manifest-file, which would point version lookups at a custom URL, is unset, so the bundled manifest is used
not_reviewed: dist/setup/index.cjs and dist/save-cache/index.cjs -- both bundles unread. In particular what the post: hook does with the token, and what it writes into the cache

whether the downloaded uv binary is checksum-verified internally by default. The action offers a `checksum` input, we pass none, and the bundle that would do any default verification is unread -- so this record claims no verification, in either direction
bounded_by: runs in the static-analysis job, which declares no job-level permissions and so inherits the workflow's top-level contents: read -- no write anywhere
SHA-pinned with a version comment, asserted by tests/security/test_workflow_permissions.py

the only thing run with the installed uv is `uv lock --check`; scripts/check_locks.py independently verifies the exported pip locks against uv.lock, so a tampered resolver would have to satisfy that gate too
actions.notes: Reviewed at the pinned SHA on 2026-11-05 -- the pin #317 landed. The finding worth an owner decision is the unpinned download: we pass no `checksum`, and the mirror is the default source. Setting `checksum` would close it, at the cost of an input to update on every version bump. Also carried forward from the execution block: the post: hook runs after the job with the same token and nobody has read it -- the penthera record verifies the ABSENCE of such a hook, so the property matters here.

actions.reason: One of the two required secret scanners (AGENTS.md §8 stage 3). Predates this file.
properties_verified: runs.using is node24 with a single entrypoint, dist/index.js: no Docker image, so the 40-hex pin fixes the code that runs
no pre: or post: hooks
the action declares NO inputs at all -- its only top-level keys are name, author, branding, description and runs -- so no `with:` value can reach it, and our step passes none

LICENCE: a proprietary Gitleaks LLC end-user licence agreement, NOT open source. The action.yml header reads 'Copyright (c) 2022 Gitleaks LLC - All Rights Reserved' and points at gitleaks.io/COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.txt. This differs from `gitleaks` the scanner, which is MIT

per its README at the pinned SHA, a licence key is required for ORGANIZATION-owned repositories and 'not required for user accounts'; this repository is user-owned and our step sets no GITLEAKS_LICENSE
per the same README, GITHUB_TOKEN is used 'to call a GitHub API to comment on PRs', and the only third-party data it claims to send is licence-key validation traffic
not_reviewed: dist/index.js, the bundled driver -- not read. It is proprietary, so auditing it is licence-constrained as well as impractical, and this record does not claim otherwise
whether the vendor's 'only licence-validation data leaves' claim holds, since the bundle is unread. It is recorded as the vendor's claim, not as a verified property
what it actually does with the GITHUB_TOKEN it is handed
bounded_by: the security job holds contents: read and pull-requests: READ -- no write anywhere, so the token it receives cannot comment or modify despite the README saying it comments on PRs
GITLEAKS_VERSION: 8.30.1 pins the scanner binary it fetches
SHA-pinned with a version comment, asserted by tests/security/test_workflow_permissions.py
actions.notes: Reviewed at the pinned SHA on 2026-11-05. Two things an operator should carry forward. FIRST, this is the only PROPRIETARY dependency in the tree: AGENTS.md section 4 requires a dependency's licence to be justified, and this one never was -- whether a commercial EULA belongs in a portfolio repository whose own code is Apache-2.0 is the owner's call, not a defect. SECOND, an operational cliff: the licence key is free but REQUIRED for an organization account, so moving this repository under a GitHub organization breaks the required secret-scanning check (section 8 stage 3) until a key is obtained. Counter-note to the bounds above, stated because it is the opposite of a bound: this IS a required check, so a compromised release could not write anything but could deny every merge.

actions.reason: OpenSSF Scorecard reporting. Predates this file.

execution.pin_gap: A Docker action whose image is referenced by the MUTABLE tag v2.5.0, not by a sha256 digest. Our 40-hex pin fixes action.yaml; action.yaml names an image, so the pin does not fix the code that runs. Whoever can push that tag in ghcr.io/ossf chooses the container this repository executes. Alone among the four records here. NOT closed -- referencing the image by digest is upstream's to do -- but now DETECTED: image_digest below is the digest the tag resolved to when measured, and the image-pin job re-resolves it and fails before the analysis job runs. Detection is the weaker property and is recorded as the weaker one: a moved tag is caught on the next run of that workflow, not prevented.

properties_verified: runs.using is docker with image: docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.5.0 -- a MUTABLE tag, so the 40-hex pin does NOT fix the code that runs. See execution.pin_gap; the image-pin job watches it
seven inputs: results_file and results_format (both required), repo_token, publish_results, file_mode, internal_publish_base_url, internal_default_token
internal_publish_base_url defaults to "https://api.scorecard.dev", which is the egress endpoint tests/security/test_scorecard_boundary.py asserts and the one shown for the section 5.1 approval
publish_results defaults to false AND our step sets it to false explicitly, so the decision is recorded rather than inherited
BOTH repo_token and internal_default_token default to ${{ github.token }}, so the container receives the job's token
top-level keys are name, description, author, inputs, branding, runs -- no nested action and no composite steps
not_reviewed: the action's own definition has been read, but the CONTENTS of ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.5.0 have not -- for a Docker action the image IS the code, and it cannot be read from this repository
the contents of that image are additionally not pinned by our SHA, see execution.pin_gap
what the container does with the token it receives
bounded_by: the workflow is not one of section 8's required checks; it runs on a schedule and on push
the image-pin job re-resolves the tag and the analysis job needs: it, so a moved tag fails before the image is pulled for analysis
top-level permissions are contents: read and the job adds exactly one write
actions.notes: Reviewed at the pinned SHA on 2026-11-05. NEW FINDING, recorded rather than fixed: the analysis job holds security-events: write for the SEPARATE upload-sarif step, and a workflow token is job-scoped -- so the scorecard container also receives a token carrying that write, through the two token-defaulted inputs above, for an upload it does not perform. Narrowing it means splitting the job: run scorecard under contents: read and publish the SARIF as an artifact, then upload to code scanning from a second job holding the write. That is a workflow change with its own boundary test, not part of a review, so it is written down here instead of done. The mutable-tag gap is unchanged and still upstream's to close.
